correctness.rationale: For any affine plane q>=2, graph distances and uniqueness show K=U cup V with intersection exactly incidence graph G. Each line vertex is dominated in U, hence U contractible; each point vertex is dominated in V, hence V collapses to the line-only complex B. B is join of q+1 q-point sets, hence simply connected wedge of (q-1)^(q+1) q-spheres. As G is connected one-dimensional, its map to B is nullhomotopic. The cofibration pushout splits K as B wedge Sigma G. The graph has q^2(q+1) edges and 2q^2+q vertices, so the cycle rank is (q-1)^2(q+1), yielding the claimed two-sphere summands. Exhaustive actual verifier checks for q=2,3 compute full maximal-clique complex and mod-two homology consistent with the theorem; finite cases are not used to justify universality. q=2 dimension coincidence addressed. No other hidden lemma required.

originality.rationale: The all-plane mixed-dimensional formula differs structurally from the published projective-plane q^3 two-sphere result: disjoint affine parallel classes force a noncontractible join B. Full inspected primary texts by Larrión et al and Kawamura give only pi1/relative equivalence comparisons and neither implies these two absolute ranks. The 2025 topological Rips paper supplies a current setting but not a finite affine computation. value.rationale: Affine planes are a canonical family of incidence geometries, including non-Desarguesian examples. The formula is an exact integral homotopy-type classification across every existing order, not a finite table or a cosmetic parameter substitution. The extra q-dimensional wedge from parallel classes is a genuinely different geometric feature absent in projective planes, gives nontrivial homology in arbitrarily high dimensions for prime-power orders, and supplies natural explicit metric-space Rips benchmarks. The q=2 and q=3 computations verify the nontrivial dimension-coincidence and dimension-separation boundaries.
